test_title: PYST 12: SSC CHSL - General Awareness (Held on: 13 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements regarding the Deccan Plateau is NOT correct?

options.text: The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.
The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass.
An extension of the Plateau is also visible in the northeast.
The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west.

solution:
**The correct answer is 'The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deccan Plateau:**

 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau located in southern India, characterized by its high altitude and rich volcanic soil, which supports diverse flora and fauna.
 
• This plateau is primarily a segment of the ancient Gondwanaland and includes parts of eight Indian states, stretching from the Satpura Range in the north to the Southern Indian ranges of the Eastern and Western Ghats.
 
• The plateau covers approximately 500,000 square kilometers, making it one of the largest plateaus in the world.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards, a characteristic that influences the flow of many rivers originating in the west and draining eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This eastward slope is due to tectonic activity and the ancient geological processes that have shaped the land over millions of years.
 
• It forms a roughly triangular landmass, bounded by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges to the north, the Eastern Ghats to the east, and the Western Ghats to the west.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extension to the Northeast:**

 
 
• An extension of the Deccan Plateau is also visible in the northeast, where it merges into the Chota Nagpur Plateau. This area, rich in minerals, is crucial for India's mining industry.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Statement about the Satpura Range:**
 
 
• The Satpura range does not flank the Deccan Plateau’s broad base in the west. Instead, it is situated to the north of the plateau and runs parallel to the Vindhya Range. Together, they demarcate the boundary between the Indo-Gangetic plains and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The Western Ghats, a continuous range running parallel to the western coast of India, is the range that borders the Deccan Plateau on the west.
 
 
 
• **Western and Eastern Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are known for their biodiversity and are a UNESCO World Heritage site. They rise steeply from the west coast and descend gently towards the plateau.
 
• The Eastern Ghats are a series of discontinuous hills and mountains that run along India's eastern coast. These ranges are lower in elevation compared to the Western Ghats and are less continuous.
